title: Enneacraft - a practical flip-control course
description: An original MDPro4 teaching sheet: two exact openings, four flip-control tools, every Enneacraft response, and the resource loop that turns small advantages into a finish. Start with Openings, then learn one interaction at a time. Some guides begin from an established board rather than an opening hand; their captions say so. Conditional outcomes are not combined into an imaginary endboard. Read the card text, costs, turn and chain conditions before acting. Deck-copy counts are explicit wherever a random reveal is made deterministic. The guides use the installed card effects and scripts; annotated teaching diagrams are not executable replays.
author: MDPro4 - original guide

combos.title: Two cards: prepare Atori for the next summon
combos.description: An exact low-investment opening with Proto and Atori in hand. Keep all 3 copies of Reverth in the Deck to make the first search deterministic, and have more than 900 LP. The unknown draw is a bonus, not a promised combo piece. This line gives one conditional opponent-turn interruption and preserves your Normal Summon; it does not establish an unbreakable board.

cardNotes.end:54842941: Face-down Defense Position; waiting for Reverth
cardNotes.end:80015408: Ready when the opponent successfully summons

steps.title: Scale Proto and find Reverth
steps.text: Place Proto in a Pendulum Zone. Pay 900 LP for its Pendulum Effect. Reveal 3 copies of Reverth still in the Deck, so the random choice must be Reverth. If you cannot reveal all 3, this exact line is no longer guaranteed.

steps.title: Exchange the used scale
steps.text: Activate Reverth. Shuffle the face-up Proto from your Pendulum Zone into the Main Deck and draw 1 card. Keep Atori in hand. Do not assume what you draw, and do not shuffle away Atori for this line.

steps.title: Set Atori with its own hand effect
steps.text: Reveal Atori and activate its hand effect; Special Summon that same Atori face-down. You must not have Special Summoned anything face-up earlier this turn, and cannot do so afterward. This is an effect Special Summon, not a Pendulum Summon. The Normal Summon remains available.

steps.title: Pass with the correct expectation
steps.text: Atori cannot use its Quick Effect during the opponent's turn. Your interaction is Reverth in the GY: after an opponent's Normal or Special Summon outside the Damage Step, it can flip Atori. Do not count a second negate or assume Atori reacts to every action.

flow.caption: Set monster, not an opponent-turn omni-negate

steps.title: Use Reverth after a successful summon
steps.text: When its GY trigger is offered, banish Reverth and choose the effect that turns a face-down Enneacraft face-up. Select Atori at resolution. This is a response to a successful summon, not a summon negation, so the opponent can also have summon triggers.

steps.title: Resolve the separate Flip Effect
steps.text: After that chain finishes, resolve Atori's Flip Effect on the next chain. It changes opposing monsters that can be changed to face-down Defense Position and prevents those changed monsters from changing battle position. Link Monsters cannot be changed face-down; unaffected monsters may remain face-up. Earlier summon effects were not retroactively negated.

flow.caption: Next chain: flip the opposing board down

combos.title: Three cards: Atori, a counter scale and Enneapolis
combos.description: A complete Proto + Deftero + Atori opening with no dependence on a favorable draw. The Deck must contain 3 Reset, 3 Reverth and at least 1 Enneapolis. Both Level 1 Pendulum Effects must resolve, and you need more than 1800 LP. It adds resource recovery and counter damage to the smaller Atori line.

steps.title: First name finds Reset
steps.text: Scale Proto. Pay 900 LP and reveal 3 Reset from the Deck; the randomly chosen card is therefore Reset. Do not use a mixed reveal pile and call the result guaranteed.

steps.title: Second name finds Reverth
steps.text: Scale Deftero in the other Pendulum Zone. Pay another 900 LP and reveal 3 Reverth. Proto and Deftero are different names, so each can use its search once. Returning either to hand will not reset that name's once-per-turn search.

steps.title: Place Enneapolis
steps.text: Activate Reset and choose its field-placement effect. Place Enneapolis from the Deck in your Field Zone. Reset goes to the GY after the chain; its GY effect can be useful later, but requires an occupied Pendulum Zone and a face-up Enneacraft monster.

steps.title: Return both used scales
steps.text: Use Enneapolis's ignition effect, target Proto and Deftero in your Pendulum Zones, and return both to hand. This is the Field Spell's once-per-turn mass-return effect, separate from its once-per-turn response to a flip.

steps.title: Load Reverth without gambling on the draw
steps.text: Activate Reverth. Shuffle only Proto from your hand into the Deck and draw 1. Keep Deftero and Atori. The endpoint needs neither the drawn card nor another search.

steps.title: Use Deftero to set Atori
steps.text: Reveal Deftero in hand to Special Summon Atori from hand face-down. Keep Deftero in hand after its effect. Respect the whole-turn restriction against face-up Special Summons.

steps.title: Restore one counter scale
steps.text: Place Deftero back in a Pendulum Zone. Its search was already used, so do not pay for another. With 8000 starting LP and no other changes, you now have 6200 LP. Your Normal Summon is still unused.

steps.title: Spend the next turn carefully
steps.text: After an opponent summons, Reverth can flip Atori and Atori's separate Flip Effect can turn their board down. Deftero gains 1 counter for that flip event. You may decline Enneapolis's optional flip-response to keep Atori on the field. Reset can later re-set a face-up Enneacraft after an eligible opposing activation; it is not a free effect you can use at any time.

flow.caption: Flip and trigger on the following chain
One counter for this flip event

combos.title: Proto before a search: respond to Ash or Droll
combos.description: A conditional sequencing lesson, not protection from every hand trap. Start with Proto plus a different Level 1 name in hand and a useful Enneacraft search target in the Deck. Normal Set Proto before the other name searches. The opponent must actually use an eligible monster effect in hand; do not invent that response.

cardNotes.end:56187077: Face-up after responding; Flip Effect is a later chain
cardNotes.end:54020393: Example follow-up search; actual choice is yours

endFlow.caption: Face-up after responding; Flip Effect is a later chain
Example follow-up search; actual choice is yours

steps.title: Normal Set Proto first
steps.text: Use your Normal Set on Proto. Then place Deftero in a Pendulum Zone and activate its paid search. This preserves Proto's face-down response to a monster effect activated in the opponent's hand.

flow.caption: Normal Set: uses the Normal Summon/Set

steps.title: Ash branch: get a separate search
steps.text: If Ash chains to Deftero as Chain Link 2, chain Proto as Chain Link 3. Proto flips face-up as the activation cost, then its effect searches an Enneacraft such as Release. Ash still negates Deftero's original search if it resolves. Proto does not negate Ash.

flow.caption: Opponent CL2: negate the original search
Your CL3: flip and search separately

steps.title: Droll branch: the response can resolve first
steps.text: If the first search resolved and Droll is activated in a later chain, Proto can respond directly. Proto's search resolves before Droll applies its restriction. Once Droll has resolved, stop planning further Main Deck searches or draws. Release can still place a monster directly into a Pendulum Zone.

flow.caption: Direct response searches before Droll resolves

steps.title: Separate the destruction from the search
steps.text: Proto's mandatory Flip Effect starts a later chain and destroys an opposing monster if one is available. It does not destroy the hand trap after that hand trap has gone to the GY. If the opponent has no monster, there is no destruction payoff.

steps.title: Know what does not qualify
steps.text: Proto responds to a monster effect activated in hand. It cannot respond to a Trap merely because that Trap was activated from hand. An intervening chain link can also prevent a when-response to the earlier effect. If no hand trap is used, Proto simply remains Set.

flow.caption: Check the most recent activation, not just its animation

combos.title: Sol and Luna: flip Atori and disrupt twice
combos.description: Begin with Atori face-down and Sol and Luna already Set from a previous turn for use on the opponent's turn. The opponent must control a targetable monster whose position can be changed. This route works without waiting for Atori's own Quick Effect condition.

cardNotes.start:19739265: Already Set; legal to activate this turn
cardNotes.start:0: Opponent has a legal position-change target
cardNotes.end:0: Affected opposing monsters face-down and position-locked

Opponent has a legal position-change target

endFlow.caption: Face-up Defense Position

steps.title: Choose one target on each side
steps.text: Activate Sol and Luna, targeting your face-down Atori and one opposing face-up monster that can be changed face-down. Both sides must have a legal target at activation; an opposing Link Monster is not a suitable face-up target.

flow.caption: Target one monster on each side
Opponent face-up target; not a Link

steps.title: Resolve each remaining target
steps.text: Sol and Luna changes a face-down target to face-up Defense Position and a face-up target to face-down Defense Position. It checks the target's position at resolution. A target that leaves the field is not changed; the other related target can still be changed.

steps.title: Use Atori on the next chain
steps.text: Atori's Flip Effect activates after the current chain. It turns the opponent's other eligible face-up monsters face-down and locks the positions of monsters it changed. The monster already turned down by Sol and Luna was not changed by Atori and does not receive Atori's position lock from this resolution.

flow.caption: Separate chain: flip remaining eligible monsters
Already face-down Sol target: no Atori lock from this effect

steps.title: Do not mistake this for negation
steps.text: Flipping a monster down does not automatically negate its already-activated effect. This can deny later face-up effects, material use or attacks, but resolve the original chain normally. Sol and Luna is once per turn; Atori's own Flip Effect has no printed once-per-turn limit.

flow.caption: Position disruption, not a retroactive negate

combos.title: Book of Moon: reuse a face-up Enneacraft
combos.description: A short reset line for a face-up Deftero that has already used its response. Have Book of Moon legally available; on the opponent's turn it normally must have been Set earlier. This prepares another response, but cannot force the opponent to search.

cardNotes.start:92171126: Face-up monster; previous response already resolved
cardNotes.end:92171126: Face-down again; waiting for an eligible opposing effect

startFlow.caption: Face-up monster; previous response already resolved

endFlow.caption: Face-down again; waiting for an eligible opposing effect

steps.title: Turn your own monster down
steps.text: Activate Book of Moon targeting your face-up Deftero. If it remains a legal, related face-up target, change it to face-down Defense Position.

steps.title: Wait for a new qualifying activation
steps.text: If the opponent later activates an effect that adds from Deck to hand, Deftero can respond while face-down: flip it up and search an Enneacraft. Book did not itself provide a second search; the opponent's later activation is required.

flow.caption: New eligible response: flip and search

steps.title: Resolve the hand disruption separately
steps.text: After the chain, Deftero's Flip Effect banishes one random card from the opponent's hand face-up until the End Phase. It is temporary, and you do not choose the card. An empty opposing hand gives no hand-removal result.

flow.caption: Mandatory Flip Effect on a new chain
Random opposing hand card; returns at End Phase

steps.title: Book cannot flip Atori up
steps.text: Book of Moon only changes face-up monsters face-down. Use Sol and Luna or Reverth to turn a Set Atori face-up on the opponent's turn. Resetting a Level 1 monster also does not reset its named Pendulum search limit.

flow.caption: Alternative for turning a Set monster face-up

combos.title: Daruma: reset your monster, then remove remaining face-up cards
combos.description: Start with a legal Set Daruma and at least one face-up monster that its effect can actually turn face-down. Your own face-up Enneacraft can supply that requirement against opposing Links or unaffected monsters. Do not activate on a board where no monster can be turned face-down.

steps.title: Check the first part can succeed
steps.text: Confirm that at least one face-up monster can become face-down. A Link Monster cannot, and immunity may prevent the change. A face-down Enneacraft is not enough by itself because it is already down.

steps.title: Resolve the position change
steps.text: Activate Daruma. It turns as many monsters as possible face-down, including your face-up Enneacraft. If zero monsters are successfully turned down, stop: the send-to-GY part does not happen.

steps.title: Apply the player action
steps.text: After a successful change, each player with face-up monsters sends all of those face-up monsters to the GY. This can remove Links and monsters unaffected by activated effects because the instruction is applied to the player. It is not destruction and affects your remaining face-up monsters too.

flow.caption: Remaining face-up monsters are sent by their controller

steps.title: Resume the control loop
steps.text: Your surviving face-down Enneacrafts are ready for later matching activations. Daruma did not flip them face-up, so it did not itself trigger their Flip Effects or create E.C. Counters. It also does not undo effects that already resolved.

flow.caption: Ready for a later qualifying response

combos.title: Book of Eclipse: a temporary opening with an End Phase cost
combos.description: Use Eclipse when turning the field down now is worth the opponent's possible End Phase draws. Begin with a face-up Enneacraft and a legally available Eclipse. This is a board-state lesson, not a guaranteed combo or a replacement for Daruma's send effect.

cardNotes.start:35480699: Available now; must be Set earlier on opponent turn
cardNotes.start:92171126: Face-up monster you want to re-set

endFlow.caption: Your monster stays face-down unless another effect flips it

steps.title: Turn eligible monsters down
steps.text: Activate Eclipse. Its effect turns eligible face-up monsters on both sides face-down without targeting. It does not turn Links face-down or send them away. Ash can negate Eclipse because its effect includes drawing.

flow.caption: Change eligible face-up monsters on both sides

steps.title: Use the window, not an imaginary permanent lock
steps.text: Face-down opposing monsters may lose access to face-up effects and certain summon uses. Their already-activated effects are not automatically negated. If you have real removal or a legal winning line, use it before the End Phase; do not assume the opponent remains locked.

steps.title: Account for the delayed flip and draw
steps.text: At the End Phase, Eclipse tries to turn as many opposing face-down monsters as possible face-up, then the opponent draws for the number actually turned up. This can include monsters that were already Set before Eclipse. Your own monsters are not turned up by this delayed effect.

flow.caption: Opponent flips up, then draws for actual changes

steps.title: Count damage correctly
steps.text: Those flips can add counters to your occupied Enneacraft scales. But an opposing draw caused by your Eclipse is not caused by the opponent's own card effect, so your Aiza.LEON does not burn them for that draw. Do not advertise Eclipse plus LEON as automatic draw damage.

flow.caption: No burn for draws caused by your Eclipse
May use counters from those flip events

steps.title: Proto: hand monster effects
steps.text: Respond to an opposing monster effect activated in hand. Flip Proto face-up as the cost and search an Enneacraft on resolution. On the following chain, its Flip Effect destroys an opposing monster if possible. A Trap activation from hand is not a monster effect.

steps.title: Deftero: Deck-to-hand effects
steps.text: Respond to an opposing effect that includes adding from Deck to hand, including an appropriate draw effect. Search on resolution. Its later Flip Effect temporarily banishes a random opposing hand card face-up until the End Phase. It is neither permanent nor chosen removal.

flow.caption: Deck-to-hand response; later temporary hand disruption

steps.title: Ekto: effects that Special Summon
steps.text: Respond to an opposing card or effect that includes Special Summoning. Search, then use the later Flip Effect to negate one opposing Effect Monster for the rest of the turn. A summon without an activated effect is not a trigger for this Quick Effect. Summon-trigger effects may resolve before Ekto's later negation.

steps.title: Enato: GY or banishment effects
steps.text: Respond to an opposing card effect activated in the GY or banishment. Search, then shuffle up to 3 opposing cards from the GY and/or banishment into the Deck with the later Flip Effect. The original effect has already had its chance to resolve, so do not promise to stop it by shuffling its card afterward.

flow.caption: GY/banishment activation; later recycle up to 3 opposing cards

steps.title: Trito: effects that Set cards
steps.text: Respond to an opposing effect that includes Setting a card. Search first. On the later chain, destroy an opposing Spell/Trap; only if that destruction succeeds does Trito then Special Summon a monster from your hand face-down. The Flip Effect is mandatory even when your hand has no summonable monster.

flow.caption: Setting-effect response; destroy backrow, then summon

steps.title: Keep the timing honest
steps.text: Their quick searches require a legal matching activation and an available search. Face-up copies cannot pay the flip-up cost again. Re-setting a monster can enable another response because these monster effects have no once-per-turn limit; it does not reset the named once-per-turn Pendulum search.

combos.title: Atori on your turn: negate a field activation, then flip the board
combos.description: Set Atori before asking the opponent to use a field effect. Its Quick Effect is live only on your turn and must respond to an opposing activation on the field. This lesson starts from an already Set Atori and does not assume the opponent cooperates.

cardNotes.start:54842941: Already Set; it is your turn
cardNotes.start:0: Opponent activates an eligible card/effect on the field
cardNotes.end:0: Opponent activation negated; eligible board turned down

startFlow.caption: Already Set; it is your turn
Opponent activates an eligible card/effect on the field

endFlow.caption: Face-up after its response
Opponent activation negated; eligible board turned down

steps.title: Identify the actual activation location
steps.text: During your turn, wait for an opposing card or effect activated on the field. A monster effect activated in hand or GY does not qualify. A Trap activated from hand is activated onto the field, but still respect response restrictions and Spell Speed.

flow.caption: Your turn plus opposing field activation

steps.title: Flip as the response cost
steps.text: Chain Atori directly when legal. It becomes face-up Defense Position as the activation cost. Its Quick Effect negates that activation and destroys the card if it remains related. A later negation of Atori does not rewind the fact that it flipped.

flow.caption: Flip up; negate the opposing activation

steps.title: Resolve the later Flip Effect
steps.text: After the chain, Atori's mandatory Flip Effect gets its own chain. Turn opposing monsters that can be affected face-down and apply its battle-position restriction to those actually changed. This second effect can still be negated or prevented independently.

flow.caption: Only monsters actually changed get the position restriction

steps.title: Use a different trigger next turn
steps.text: On the opponent's turn, Atori cannot use that Quick Effect. If it is re-set, use a legal Reverth or Sol and Luna flip to access its Flip Effect. Do not count its own-turn negate as a standing opponent-turn negate.

combos.title: Asta.PIXEA: respond to targeting and keep the protection
combos.description: Start with Asta.PIXEA face-down. The opponent must activate an effect targeting a card you control. This does not protect against non-targeting removal, Tributes, costs or a response you are forbidden to make.

cardNotes.start:0: Opponent effect targets a card you control
cardNotes.end:28454232: Face-up in Monster Zone: opponent cannot target field/GY cards
cardNotes.end:0: One random opposing hand card may be banished face-down

startFlow.caption: Opponent effect targets a card you control

endFlow.caption: Face-up in Monster Zone: opponent cannot target field/GY cards
One random opposing hand card may be banished face-down

steps.title: Check that your card is actually targeted
steps.text: Read the target selection of the opposing activation. Asta responds when at least one target is a card you control. A card that merely chooses at resolution does not target. A targeting effect aimed only at a GY card does not satisfy the condition of targeting a card you control.

flow.caption: Must be face-down with a qualifying latest activation

steps.title: Flip up and apply the continuous restriction
steps.text: Activate Asta's Quick Effect and flip it face-up as cost. After it has flipped, its continuous effect prevents the opponent from targeting cards in either field or GY while Asta remains an effective face-up monster. This protection is not a separate optional Flip Effect.

flow.caption: Flip-up cost establishes its continuous effect

steps.title: Negate the effect and optionally remove a hand card
steps.text: On resolution negate the answered effect, then you may banish one random card from the opponent's hand face-down. You cannot inspect and select the strongest card. An empty hand leaves no card to banish; there is no End Phase return clause like Deftero has.

flow.caption: Negate the effect; not its activation

steps.title: Do not re-set protection without a reason
steps.text: Turning Asta face-down prepares another response but removes its current continuous targeting protection. Weigh that cost before using Book of Moon, Reset or Daruma. Non-targeting, non-destruction removal remains a weakness.

flow.caption: Alternative: re-set to prepare a future response

combos.title: Aiza.LEON: punish a response to your own effect
combos.description: Aiza.LEON starts face-down. It can respond when the opponent chains a card or effect to your activation. You need a real opposing response; activating a card yourself does not guarantee LEON becomes usable. This line separates its bounce from its later damage effect.

cardNotes.start:0: Your effect, then an opposing response
cardNotes.end:82359538: Keep face-up to punish cards added by their own effects
cardNotes.end:0: Up to 3 eligible field cards returned on resolution

startFlow.caption: Your effect, then an opposing response

endFlow.caption: Keep face-up to punish cards added by their own effects
Up to 3 eligible field cards returned on resolution

steps.title: Build only a real chain
steps.text: For example, you activate a Level 1 Pendulum search as Chain Link 1 and the opponent uses Ash as Chain Link 2. If LEON was already face-down, it may respond as Chain Link 3. No opposing response means no LEON response from this condition.

steps.title: Choose the useful returns at resolution
steps.text: LEON flips as cost and returns up to 3 eligible cards on either field to hand when its effect resolves. It does not target. Choose opponent threats, your used scales, or endangered cards according to the actual board. Extra Deck monsters return to the Extra Deck rather than staying in hand.

flow.caption: Choose actual eligible field cards at resolution

steps.title: Do not claim that a bounce negated Ash
steps.text: Ash in the GY is not a card on the field and cannot be returned by LEON's effect. Bouncing the searched-from scale does not, by itself, negate Ash. Resolve every remaining chain link using its own rules.

flow.caption: Not a field card after its discard
Bounce is not an activation negate

steps.title: Keep LEON if damage matters
steps.text: After it has flipped, LEON in the Monster Zone deals 900 damage per card the opponent adds to their hand by their own card effects. That includes relevant draws/searches, but not their ordinary Draw Phase draw or returns caused by your LEON. Returning LEON itself removes this ongoing benefit.

flow.caption: 900 per card added by an opposing card effect

combos.title: Atil.SPIA: answer an opponent at Chain Link 3 or higher
combos.description: This is a conditional chain lesson for a Set Atil.SPIA. The opponent must activate a card/effect as Chain Link 3 or later. It cannot be activated just because a chain eventually has three links, and it does not negate your own lower links.

cardNotes.start:0: Opponent is the latest activation at CL3 or higher
cardNotes.end:71801447: Face-up; constrains opposing responses to their own effects

startFlow.caption: Opponent is the latest activation at CL3 or higher

endFlow.caption: Face-up; constrains opposing responses to their own effects
Eligible earlier opposing activations negated

steps.title: Count who activated the latest link
steps.text: Example pattern: opponent CL1, you CL2, opponent CL3. A Set SPIA can now be your CL4 if responses are permitted. Opponent CL1 followed by your CL2 does not suffice; nor can you chain to a Counter Trap with an ordinary monster Quick Effect.

flow.caption: Wait for an opposing CL3+ activation

steps.title: Flip and negate the earlier opposing links
steps.text: Flip SPIA face-up as cost. On resolution, it negates the activations of the opponent's earlier cards/effects in that chain where negation is legal, then destroys the applicable cards. Your earlier effect is not negated by SPIA.

flow.caption: Your response: negate earlier opposing activations

steps.title: Distinguish destruction from negation
steps.text: A card that moved away may no longer be destroyable by this effect, and an activation that cannot be negated is not overridden. A successful negation is not proof that every involved physical card was destroyed.

flow.caption: Check each link and each card separately

steps.title: Use the face-up restriction correctly
steps.text: After being flipped, SPIA prevents the opponent from activating cards/effects in response to their own card/effect activation while its continuous effect applies. This is not a blanket ban on their effects, and they can still respond to your activation when otherwise legal.

flow.caption: Stops their responses to their own activations

combos.title: Archa.TAIL: protect the board and count damage events
combos.description: Start with Archa.TAIL Set. Its Quick Effect answers a qualifying opposing activation that would destroy a card on the field. It grants destruction protection; it does not negate that activation. The damage effect only begins after TAIL has flipped.

cardNotes.start:0: Opponent activates an eligible destruction effect
cardNotes.end:81237046: Face-up; 900 damage per qualifying GY-send event

startFlow.caption: Opponent activates an eligible destruction effect

endFlow.caption: Face-up; 900 damage per qualifying GY-send event
Example protected Enneacraft Spell

steps.title: Check the actual destruction effect
steps.text: Respond only when the core offers TAIL for the opponent's destructive activation. Merely containing the word destroy in unrelated or optional text does not establish that this activation qualifies. Non-destruction removal is not covered.

flow.caption: Face-down and a legal destruction response

steps.title: Resolve protection, not negation
steps.text: Flip TAIL face-up as cost. Its resolving effect protects your monsters and Enneacraft Spells from card-effect destruction for the rest of this turn. Other parts of the opposing effect may still resolve; this does not protect every non-Enneacraft Spell/Trap.

flow.caption: Your monsters and Enneacraft Spells gain protection

steps.title: Count groups of monsters sent to their GY
steps.text: While the flipped TAIL remains an effective face-up monster, each event sending one or more monsters to the opponent's GY causes 900 damage. Three monsters sent together are one event for 900, not automatically 2700. Separate sends can produce separate damage.

steps.title: Keep the zones and duration distinct
steps.text: An Enneacraft Pendulum Monster going from field toward the GY normally goes face-up to the Extra Deck instead. Do not count that as a monster reaching the opponent's GY. Turning TAIL down loses its active continuous damage effect; the already-resolved turn-long protection is a different effect.

flow.caption: Continuous damage needs face-up Monster Zone
Pendulum field departure can go to face-up Extra Deck

combos.title: Enneapolis: turn flip events into a measured finish
combos.description: Begin with Enneapolis and one or two occupied Enneacraft Pendulum Zones. This is a damage accounting lesson for an established board. Nine counters are enough for 8100 damage, but Enneapolis does not require exactly nine and does not wait until you reach nine.

cardNotes.end:17621695: End Phase: remove current counters; 900 damage each
cardNotes.end:56187077: Counters are removed, not carried through this resolution

endFlow.caption: End Phase: remove current counters; 900 damage each
Counters are removed, not carried through this resolution

steps.title: Count events, not the number of flipped cards
steps.text: Each occupied Enneacraft scale gains 1 E.C. Counter each time one or more monsters are flipped face-up. A single event that flips three monsters gives each scale 1 counter, not 3. Separate flip events can each give another counter, and flips on either side can qualify.

flow.caption: Second scale also gains one per event

steps.title: Keep the counter holders on the field
steps.text: Counters sit on the Pendulum cards. Returning a scale with Enneapolis, shuffling it with Reverth, or otherwise removing it loses the counters on that card. Choose whether the extra card/resource is worth more than the pending damage.

flow.caption: Returning a scale trades away its counters
Returned card does not carry counters to hand

steps.title: Resolve the End Phase damage
steps.text: During the End Phase, Enneapolis removes all E.C. Counters currently on your field and deals 900 damage for each removed. One counter means 900; four mean 3600; nine mean 8100. Use the opponent's actual remaining LP and relevant damage prevention, not a promise of lethal.

steps.title: Use the Main Phase flip-response deliberately
steps.text: Once per turn in a Main Phase, Enneapolis can respond after your Enneacraft Pendulum monster flips and return one of those monsters to hand or place it in an open Pendulum Zone. Moving it away can sacrifice a valuable continuous effect. This newly placed scale was not already in the Pendulum Zone for the earlier flip event.

flow.caption: Optional: move one newly flipped monster
Choose hand or an open Pendulum Zone

steps.title: Do not Pendulum Summon between zero and zero
steps.text: The native Enneacraft scales are 0. Two scale-0 cards provide no Level interval for a Pendulum Summon. Build the field with hand effects, legal Normal Sets and the named support effects instead.

flow.caption: Scale 0: no legal interval between them

combos.title: Reset: reload a response without inventing a free chain
combos.description: Begin with Reset in your GY, a face-up Enneacraft monster you can turn down, and at least one occupied Pendulum Zone. Reset's GY effect is conditional on an opponent activation. Its exact offer belongs to the trigger window the core presents; it is not an unrestricted Quick Effect.

cardNotes.end:92171126: Face-down; can answer a later qualifying activation

endFlow.caption: Face-down; can answer a later qualifying activation
Banished as cost

steps.title: Wait for the eligible opposing activation
steps.text: An opponent must activate a card/effect outside the Damage Step while Reset is in the GY. In the installed rules, Reset is a delayed trigger offered after that chain finishes, not a Quick Effect chained directly to the activation. You cannot activate it simply because your own Flip Effect is on a chain or because you want to re-set a monster.

flow.caption: Delayed trigger after the opposing activation chain

steps.title: Keep a scale and a face-up monster available
steps.text: Banish Reset as cost when you use the effect. At resolution, the number of cards still occupying your Pendulum Zones determines how many face-up Enneacraft monsters you can turn down, up to that number. With no occupied scale at resolution, it cannot re-set any.

flow.caption: Must still occupy a Pendulum Zone

steps.title: Select the monster whose next response matters
steps.text: Turn Deftero face-down to prepare for another opposing Deck-to-hand effect, or choose another eligible Enneacraft for its own condition. Its monster effects have no printed once-per-turn limit, but the next activation still must qualify and you must have the necessary legal targets/resources.

flow.caption: Re-set; wait for another matching activation

steps.title: Understand negation and protection trade-offs
steps.text: Turning a monster down can remove applicable face-up negation, but is not a universal cure for every restriction. It also turns off continuous effects such as Asta's targeting restriction. Do not teach a specific chained negation dodge unless the actual Reset trigger window and response permissions allow it.

flow.caption: Re-setting also removes current continuous protection
Check the actual negation and response restrictions

combos.title: Release: play through a search lock and recover next turn
combos.description: Start with Release in hand, Enneapolis already face-up with its return effect unused, and an open Pendulum Zone. This demonstrates placement under Droll and later face-up Extra Deck recovery. The later recovery requires a suitable card to actually reach the face-up Extra Deck.

cardNotes.end:54842941: Example monster returned from its placed Pendulum Zone
cardNotes.end:54020393: GY effect only from a later turn

endFlow.caption: Example monster returned from its placed Pendulum Zone
GY effect only from a later turn

steps.title: Place directly from the Deck
steps.text: Activate Release with an open Pendulum Zone. Place an Enneacraft Pendulum Monster, such as Atori, directly from the Deck there. This is not a Deck-to-hand add, so an already-resolved Droll does not prohibit that placement. It also is not a Special Summon.

flow.caption: Place directly; do not search to hand

steps.title: Return the placed monster with Enneapolis
steps.text: Use Enneapolis's unused ignition effect to target and return the placed Atori to hand. Returning a field card is not adding from the Main Deck, so Droll does not stop this. You have consumed the Field Spell's mass-return use for the turn.

steps.title: Use the recovered monster within the summon lock
steps.text: If no face-up Special Summon occurred this turn, Atori can use its own hand effect to Special Summon itself face-down. The whole-turn restriction still applies. Droll does not turn this into a face-up Extra Deck summon route.

flow.caption: Reveal, then Special Summon itself face-down

steps.title: Recover a face-up Extra Deck card on a later turn
steps.text: From a later turn than the one Release reached the GY, banish Release to add one of your face-up Enneacraft Pendulum Monsters from the Extra Deck to hand. You need an actual qualifying card there; this is not a recovery from the GY, Deck or banishment.

flow.caption: Later turn only: banish from GY
Example face-up Extra Deck card returns to hand

combos.title: Trito and Enneapolis: make room before the summon
combos.description: An advanced position lesson: Trito has just flipped in the Main Phase while you control Enneapolis with its flip-response unused. You have a summonable monster in hand and the opponent has a Spell/Trap that Trito can destroy. It can work with all your Monster Zones occupied by returning Trito before its mandatory Flip Effect resolves.

cardNotes.start:44716748: Just flipped face-up in the Main Phase
cardNotes.start:0: Opponent Spell/Trap that can actually be destroyed
cardNotes.end:54842941: Special Summoned face-down into the freed zone

startFlow.caption: Just flipped face-up in the Main Phase
Opponent Spell/Trap that can actually be destroyed

endFlow.caption: Returned to hand by Enneapolis
Special Summoned face-down into the freed zone

steps.title: Recognize the two triggers
steps.text: After Trito has flipped, its mandatory Flip Effect will be placed on the next chain. Enneapolis can also trigger in the Main Phase. In a simple chain with only your two triggers, Trito is CL1 and your optional Enneapolis response is CL2; other simultaneous triggers can change the complete chain layout.

steps.title: Return Trito before its effect resolves
steps.text: Resolve Enneapolis first and return the just-flipped Trito to hand. This opens a Monster Zone. Use the flip-response, not the Field Spell's ignition effect, which cannot simply be chained here.

flow.caption: Return to hand; free a Monster Zone

steps.title: Destroy before attempting the summon
steps.text: Resolve Trito's Flip Effect: destroy an opposing Spell/Trap. If destruction succeeds, Special Summon an eligible monster from hand face-down, such as Atori, into the now-open zone. If the Spell/Trap cannot be destroyed or disappears, do not claim the summon happens anyway.

flow.caption: Resolving Flip Effect after leaving the field

steps.title: Keep the endpoint modest
steps.text: Atori is now Set, not face-up, so this summon did not trigger its Flip Effect. You still need its own eligible response on your turn or a separate legal flip effect later. Trito in hand can be reused on a future legal main-phase line.

flow.caption: Set body; no automatic Atori Flip Effect yet
